clue.text: Formality to secure treatment for swelling?

parts.note: icy reserve or stiff coldness of manner is ice, as in breaking the ice
to bag something is to capture or secure it

explanation.surface: Someone insists on a bit of paperwork before treating an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Formality' looks like red tape, but it is cold reserve of manner, ICE; 'to secure' is BAG, as in bagging a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A pack of cold ice in a bag is held against an injury to reduce inflammation.

clue.text: Cloche awry over a part of the ear

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the next one
awry means twisted out of shape, so the letters of the word cloche are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bell-shaped hat sits crooked over someone's ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awry' rearranges CLOCHE into COCHLE; 'over' puts that above A in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiral cavity of the inner ear that turns sound vibrations into nerve signals.

clue.text: Stud manager

explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a raised ornamental knob, also called a boss; a boss is also the person in charge at work.

clue.text: Composer upset whingers

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disordered, so the letters of whingers are scrambled

explanation.surface: A composer is annoyed by people who keep complaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' asks for the letters of WHINGERS to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: George Gershwin was the American who wrote Rhapsody in Blue.

clue.text: Turn into insect after swallowing good deal of honey source

indicators.note: swallowing means taking something inside, so one piece goes within the insect

parts.note: the bee is the insect that makes honey

indicators.note: a good deal of a thing is most of it, so the honey source loses its final letter

parts.note: honeycomb, or comb, is where bees store their honey

explanation.surface: A bee eats so much honey that it seems to turn into something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good deal of' drops the last letter of the honey source before 'swallowing' puts it in the insect; 'after' is only a link, and the surface's honey makes BEE easy to find.
explanation.definitionFit: To become something is to turn into it, as a caterpillar does a butterfly.

clue.text: Accessory more expensive? I don't want to hear any more!

definitions.text: I don't want to hear any more!

parts.note: a belt is a fashion accessory worn round the waist
when prices are up they are higher

explanation.surface: A shopper is told an accessory has gone up in price and snaps back.
explanation.walkthrough: BELT UP is British slang for 'shut up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rude command to be quiet, a slang way of telling someone to stop talking.

clue.text: What Tom associates with John?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat and a john is slang for a toilet, so this is what a cat uses as its loo

explanation.surface: A question about which friends Tom keeps company with.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom and John look like two men's names; tom is a male cat and john a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Granules spread in a tray where a pet relieves itself indoors.

clue.text: Damage can, one supplying drink

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
a tin is a metal can
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone dents a can while handing out drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supplying' is only a link between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail of gin and vermouth, often served with an olive.

clue.text: Lancaster, possibly associated with historic times

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of Lancaster may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: The city or royal house of Lancaster is linked with history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' asks for the letters of LANCASTER to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestral things come from forebears, belonging to earlier generations.

clue.text: Former cadets, losing little time, possibly becoming military types

indicators.note: possibly signals that the remaining letters may be rearranged into another phrase
losing means a letter is dropped from the word cadets

parts.note: t is the short form of time

explanation.surface: Ex-cadets, given a little time, may turn into soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes T from CADETS to leave CADES; 'possibly' rearranges FORMER CADES. 'becoming' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The army, navy and air force together are a nation's fighting services.

clue.text: Body also incorporating Royal Society

indicators.note: incorporating means taking something into the body, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: too means also
RS is the abbreviation for the Royal Society, Britain's science academy

explanation.surface: A learned body also includes the Royal Society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body' looks like an organisation, as the Royal Society is, but it is the trunk of a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the human frame, without head or limbs.

clue.text: Being like a tired kangaroo is prohibited

explanation.definitionFit: A worn-out kangaroo has finished all its leaps; a place forbidden to enter is off limits.

clue.text: Type of pig not particularly pleasant to mate?

definitions.text: Type of pig not particularly pleasant to mate?

parts.words: Type of pig not particularly pleasant to mate?
parts.note: reads like a farm animal unpleasant to breed with, but describes a sexist man who looks down on women, called a pig

explanation.surface: A breeder warns that one kind of pig is a poor partner for mating.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'male chauvinist pig' is a 1970s insult for a sexist man; 'mate' is a partner, not breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who believes men are superior to women is insulted as this sort of pig.

clue.text: See 11
Decisive drink (a second's left unfinished)

parts.note: a dram is a small drink of spirits

indicators.note: left unfinished means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a tick is a moment or second

explanation.surface: A drinker leaves a second glass half-drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left unfinished' cuts TICK to TIC; DRAM + A + TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatic change is striking and sudden, one that settles matters.

clue.text: It takes no pluck to play so lightweight an instrument

definitions.text: It takes no pluck to play so lightweight an instrument

parts.words: It takes no pluck to play so lightweight an instrument
parts.note: pluck looks like courage, but no strings are plucked, and the instrument is light because it is imaginary

explanation.surface: Playing such a light instrument needs no courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pluck' means courage on the surface, but also plucking strings; the instrument weighs nothing because it does not exist.
explanation.definitionFit: Miming rock guitar playing with empty hands, an instrument made only of the atmosphere.

clue.text: Article about one female offender

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the article goes round the letter for one

parts.note: the is the definite article
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A newspaper article is about a woman who broke the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside THE, then F follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A robber is a kind of criminal who steals.

clue.text: Unhappy beauty given cut flower

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling sad

indicators.note: cut means the word is shortened, losing its final letter

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A sad beauty is handed a cut flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims BELLE to BELL; 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodland plant with drooping violet bell-shaped blooms, common in British woods in spring.

clue.text: Suggest removing front from chest

indicators.note: removing the front means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: a coffer is a strongbox or chest

explanation.surface: Someone proposes taking the front panel off a chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing front from' takes C off COFFER.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose an idea is to put it forward for consideration.

clue.text: Showing enthusiasm never given free rein in newspaper

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the newspaper abbreviation

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

indicators.note: given free rein means let loose, so the letters of never run wild

explanation.surface: An enthusiast's passion never gets free rein in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given free rein' rearranges NEVER into ERVEN; 'in' puts it inside the newspaper. 'Showing enthusiasm' is an adjectival phrase, matching the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Passionate and ardent, burning with zeal.

clue.text: Outdoor scale for winds

indicators.note: winds means twists round, so the letters of scale and for are turned about

explanation.surface: A musician practises scales on wind instruments outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' looks like breezes or wind instruments, but it means twists, rearranging SCALE FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian phrase for in the fresh air, as in eating in the open.

clue.text: Chap taking in Roman Catholic when showing bitter humour

indicators.note: taking in means admitting, so the other pieces go inside the chap's name

parts.note: Sam is a man's name, a chap
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: A man lets a Catholic in while making a cutting joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' giving AS is a common crossword equivalence; 'showing' is only a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting irony that mocks, saying the opposite of what is meant.

clue.text: Father's covering up-one's not wanted

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: hair is the covering on the head

explanation.surface: A father covers up for someone who is unwelcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns HAIR to RIAH beneath PA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is a person shunned by society.

clue.text: Metal for fencing, say, right in our decorating, strangely

indicators.note: strangely signals that the letters come out in an odd new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone decorating a home oddly puts in a right angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; 'strangely' rearranges R with OUR DECORATING.
explanation.definitionFit: Wavy-ridged sheet metal often used for sheds, roofs and fences.

clue.text: See 22
Make outrageous claims, holding clothing up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: garb means clothing

explanation.surface: A boaster holds his clothes up to show off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GARB in this down entry; 'holding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To boast is to make big claims about oneself.

clue.text: Effort and energy deployed in assault on fly?

indicators.note: deployed in means placed inside, so the energy letter goes within the swipe

parts.note: a swat is a sharp blow aimed at a fly
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Lots of energy goes into trying to kill a fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed in' puts E inside SWAT; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard work makes one perspire, so the word stands for toil.

clue.text: Sweet things, diamonds, the best opening for seduction

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
the cream is the best part, as in the cream of the crop

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Diamonds and the finest things are the way to start a seduction.
explanation.walkthrough: ICE (slang for diamonds) + CREAM + S.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen desserts, a kind of confectionery.

clue.text: Leading figure associated with church shows formality

parts.note: a star is the leading figure in a show

explanation.surface: A leading figure with a church shows stiff manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'associated with' and 'shows' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiffness of manner, as in a starchy person, rigid like a stiffened collar.

clue.text: Plant to stick in place of shelter

indicators.note: in places the adhesive word inside the sheltered side

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
to gum something is to stick it

explanation.surface: Someone sticks a plant in a sheltered spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb going with 'stick', but it is the noun defined; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pod-bearing crop such as peas, beans and lentils.
